Ada Marlowe | Notes on how I work (a fictional example document for tests)

I like small tools that do one thing well. I once built a seed-swap website for my neighbourhood garden club. It had a
list, a map and a button. Forty families used it in the first month.

I explain things the way I would to a friend. I say the result first, then how I got there. When I do not know
something I say so. I do not like big words or slides full of buzzwords.
